characters.name: Samantha "Sam" Simpson
characters.description: Samantha Simpson (more commonly called "Sam") has long red hair, emerald green eyes and a green catsuit. She's the most intelligent and practical girl in the group. She pursues a Journalism major at University. Affectionate Nickname: Her friends, mainly Alex, sometimes call her "Sammy." Alliterative Name: In one episode, she presents herself as "Samantha Simpson." The show's Youtube channel would present this as her real name. Badass Bookworm: The first OP has her expertly using a chemistry kit as Clover and Alex watch her in amazement. While at the same time, she is able to fight off the random villains that the trio encounter just as effectively as her partners. AND she also manages to get and keep excellent grades at school (she's mentioned as being a straight-A student). Beware the Nice Ones: You do not want to get her angry.

characters.name: Clover Ewing
characters.description: Clover Ewing has medium blonde hair, blue eyes and a red catsuit. Probably the show's most stereotypical character, Clover is a shopping addicted, boy crazy, teenage "fashionista". She pursues a Fashion Design-major when she and her friends start college. Allergic to Routine: Clover tends gets bored rather easily. Perhaps this may explain why she has an obsession with boys... Ambition Is Evil: Clover usually tries to get famous. In fact, such a behavior is strongly explicit during the episode "Model Citizens" in which Clover and Mandy compete in a beauty contest. There are many other examples though. And Now You Must Marry Me: At least three times, a villain has kidnapped her with the intent of making her his "queen".The black knight villain in "stuck in the middle ages with you", kidnaps her and chooses her as his queen because of her beauty, though he was very sexist and would likely have treated her as another slave than a queen.Dr. Gelee in the episode "The Iceman Cometh" takes her to be his companion and "ice queen".Salty Schooner became smitten with her and tried to force her to become his "pirate queen". The black knight villain in "stuck in the middle ages with you", kidnaps her and chooses her as his queen because of her beauty, though he was very sexist and would likely have treated her as another slave than a queen.

characters.name: Alexandra "Alex" Casoy
characters.description: Alexandra Casoy (more commonly called "Alex") has short black hair, tan skin, light brown eyes and her spy catsuit is yellow. Alex is the most naive and innocent of the group, and she's interested in sports and athletics. She pursues a Veterinarian major in University. Afraid of Doctors: But not as much as she is oforthodontists; those are worse. Agent Mulder: Typically, the one to believe in curses and superstitions. Ambiguously Brown: Her skin is darker than her teammates, but her background isn't explicit. Particularly confusing because her father's skin tone changes between seasons. Her ancestry waslater confirmedto be Asian and Latin American. Angry Cheek Puff: In the early seasons, Alex puffed her cheeks on at least two different occasions when she got angry at someone; however, this gag disappeared as the series itself gradually got lessAnimesque.

characters.name: Gerald James "Jerry" Lewis
characters.description: The founder and administrator of W.O.O.H.P., the World Organization Of Human Protection, Jerry is responsible for briefing the girls on their missions. He's generally very serious and professional but he does have a sense of humour, even if it is sometimes a slightly nasty one. Accidental Pervert: A milder example, but one episode has him summon the girls early in the morning and recording their interactions with a camcorder. At one point, he does aclose uponSam, who happens to be in atowel in the process. Jerry isquite embarrassedover it. Affectionate Nickname: The girls tend to call him "Jer". Benevolent Boss: He excuses the girls from class, gives them nifty gadgets, and often sends thank-you gifts in the mail. Berserk Button: Messing with the infrastructure of WOOHP is a massive one and he had no qualms throwing hands with Lumiere as seen inA Spy Is Born II.

characters.name: Zerlina Lewis
characters.description: Affirmative-Action Legacy: Zerlina is a biracial woman who takes command of W.O.O.H.P. from her white father after he retires. Black Boss Lady: She's the leader of a spy agency and is black. Damsel in Distress: She gets captured in "Something's Fishy". Missing Mom: No one ever makes any mention about her mother, nor if Jerry ever evenhada wife. Remember the New Guy?:In-Universe. Zerlina Lewis was introduced as the new leader of W.O.O.H.P. and Jerry's adult daughter, to the girls' shock since they had been working for Jerry since they were young teenagers in high school and never once heard that he had a daughter. Jerry himself justifies this by telling the girls that he wouldn’t have been a good spy if they had known everything about him.

characters.name: Britney Akiwara
characters.description: Introduced in Seasons 2–3 as the newest recruit to the team. She was called upon everytime Alex was unavailable for a mission. All There in the Manual: Her surname is "Akiwara" according to the Finnish, Hungarian and Italian Wikipedia pages. Always Someone Better: She is very intelligent and is also very skilled, but these traits of hers made Alex become jealous of her on several occasions (believing that Britney was sent to replace her). Ambiguously Bi: Britney shows attraction to boys but also has a relationship with Alex that entails a lot ofNo Sense of Personal SpaceandpettingAlex who morphed into a kitten while she petted her. Badass in Distress: Her plane crashes on a dangerous island in her second appearance, and the girls' mission is to rescue her.

characters.name: Dean
characters.description: Debuted in the Season 3 finale. A recurring Super-Spy who helps the girls train to be better. Fake Defector: He pretends to betray the spies to Terrance to stop him.

characters.name: Blaine
characters.description: Debuted in Season 5. A seemingly normal Mali-U student who Clover has fallen head over heels in love with, but was really a rogue spy trying to take her out. This turns out to false, as his employer was Geraldine Husk, who tricked Blaine into thinking Clover was an evil spy. Butt-Monkey: Tends to get in as many mishaps as the girls do. Upon reuniting with Clover in season 7, he immediately gets kidnapped, then when on a date with her, he ends up falling down the hill. When one of the W.O.O.H.P.'s vehicles is being infiltrated by a shapeshifting villain, he's the first taken out and usurped. Long-Distance Relationship: After he and the spies take down Geraldine, he gets recruited into W.O.O.H.P., but is sent to the Australian faction, much to his and Clover's dismay. They to do this for the rest of Season 5. Butjudging by next Season, things did not work out. Mr. Fanservice: He's easy on the eyes, has a decent build, and wasintroduced shirtless. No wonder why Clover fell for him. Official Couple: After the mishap with Geraldine cleared up, he and Clover finally become one. That is, until the off-screen break up before Season 6. They seem to fall for each other again in Season 7.

characters.name: G.L.A.D.I.S.
characters.description: G.L.A.D.I.S. (Gadget Lending And Distribution Interactive System) was introduced in the episode "Physics 101 Much?" of Season 3, as a Gadget lending device. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: G.L.A.D.I.S. is usually just annoying, but not evil. However, in one episode, (at an office Christmas party that Jerry pretty much dragged the three protagonists too) she becomes homicidal after Alex spills punch on her cabinet. Jerry later admits, embarrassed, that he programmed her by downloading the intelligence from the brain of an insaneEvil Geniuswho is in prison for trying to start World War III, and when they question the inmate, they find out that he's allergic to cranberries (which make him "even crazier than usual"); Alex realizes that the punch was cranberry-flavored. The Spies are forced to accept the madman's help before G.L.A.D.I.S. carries out his original plan, which involves tricking the world's superpowers into launching its nuclear arsenals at each other. Artificial Intelligence: She appears to have a mind of her own, even sometimes claiming she's the true leader of W.O.O.H.P.. In several episodes she ignores Jerry's orders and distributes the gadgets she believes are needed for the mission. Bus Crash: She was written out of the series almost entirely due to fan complaints—in "Evil Roommate," this was written as Jerry sending G.L.A.D.I.S. to W.O.O.H.P.'s recycling facility to be dismantled. Computer Voice: She speaks with a female voice.

characters.name: Toby
characters.description: W.O.O.H.P.'s gadget maker. Artificial Limbs: Toby has a mechanical right hand. Expy: Essentially serves the same role to the girls asQ does for 007.Also subverted since Dean got that role first for one episode Gadgeteer Genius: Toby's job is to provide the various gadgets and gizmos the three leading ladies use in the field. Ship Tease: With Sam.

characters.name: Glitterstar
characters.description: Dub Name Change: She is named Mei Lin in the original French version. Foil: To Mandy. Upon discovering the girls were spies, Mandy jumped at the occasion to join their team to boss them around and bully them, and ended up hating the experience after the mission went awry, before eventually deciding to be a spy again. Glitterstar was initially distraught upon discovering her friends were spies the whole time, feeling her own life was empty and meaningless in comparison, but wound up succeeding in her mission with Toby to save the girls, eventually choosing to have her memories erased on more amiable terms. Laser-Guided Amnesia: Whenever she finds out the girls' identities, she forgets it by the end of the episode, be it by necessity or at her own request. Locked Out of the Loop: While she works for W.O.O.H.P., she's unaware of the three girls' spy activities and that her workplace is secretly managed by a spy organization. Refusal of the Call: After her mission with Toby in "Glitter Spy", she's offered a position on the Spies' team, but chooses to keep a normal life instead.

characters.name: Terrence Lewis
characters.description: Always Identical Twins: As children, they were identical, but Terry had plastic surgery as an adult — presumably because he wanted an identity outside of being Jerry's twin. Big Bad: For Season 4, anyway. Cain and Abel: The Cain to Jerry's Abel. Disproportionate Retribution: The whole reason he wants to get back at Jerry is because when they were kids, they shared their test answers, only for Jerry to turn on him when they got caught by the teacher. Apparently, this caused Terrence's life to spiral downwards. Evil Brit: And an actual Brit.

characters.name: Tim Scam
characters.description: Arch-Enemy: As their most recurring villain, he's the spies greatest enemy. He's even gone as far as to brainwash their mothers and attack them in their home. Card-Carrying Villain: In his first appearance, Clover calls him out on the scumbag he is. His response? A small "Thank you". To be fair, he's far from the only villain in the show who exhibits this behavior. Co-Dragons: With Boogie Gus and Helga Von Guggen in Season 4. Evil Genius: He's a crafty little scam artist. Freudian Excuse: Though Tim himself doesn't take it seriously, in "Mommies Dearest" he (somewhat sarcastically) says that his therapist in prison theorized that his criminal behavior stems from a lack of parental guidance. After kidnapping and brainwashing the girls mothers into taking care of his living space, he later states "If I'd known how much fun it was to have a mother, I would have stolen one long ago", which implies that he may have been an orphan or at least grew up without his mother present.

characters.name: Boogie Gus
characters.description: The '80s: A huge fan of it, so much that one of his plans involves inventing a ray capable of turning anything or anyone into a version of themselves from that era. Almighty Janitor: Before becoming a villain, he originally worked for W.O.O.H.P. as part of the custodial staff. Ascended Extra: He makes an appearance in one episode ofThe Amazing Spiez!asThe Dragonto his son, Gus Jr. Co-Dragons: With Tim Scam and Helga Von Guggen in Season 4. Disco Dan: An African-American 1970s/1980s-loving villain/former W.O.O.H.P. janitor.

characters.name: Myrna Beesbottom
characters.description: Acrofatic: Sure, she's obese but during her fight against Sam, the former demostrates herself to be very fast and agile ninja. Justified, as she was a former W.O.O.H.P. agent for 30 years. Ambition Is Evil: She becomes evil because she simply thought she could run W.O.O.H.P. better than Jerry for once avertingFreudian Excuse. A Taste of Their Own Medicine: In her second appearance, after the girls free Jerry from Myrna's love potion ring, Myrna gets a taste of her own medicine with having the ring put onherfinger instead, thus making Myrna to fall in love with herself, much to the girls' disgust. Brawn Hilda: Very muscular and heavyset yet beautiful, comely and cute. Falling-in-Love Montage: She had one with Jerry. Too bad it was all a lie.

characters.name: Helga Von Guggen
characters.description: The Dreaded: Everyone in the audience is horrified when they learn Helga was the new mystery designer "Mystique" as they all learned about herGenuine Human Hidescandal and know she's a monster. To the point the reporter on the scene immediately started telling everyone to take off their Mystique clothes figuring she must've donesomethingto them. Genuine Human Hide: Guggen transforms people intoBeast Menin an attempt to skin them alive and make clothes out of them. Her introductory episode has her showing off her latest fashion which she boasts was made out of genuine "lawyer." Hate Sink: On top of being a murderous monster, she's also a greedy, self-centered hag with no likable qualities whatsoever, not even having cool points to save her. Hoist by His Own Petard: The end of her first appearance featured her being turned into a chimera after getting submerged in the same formula she was using on her victims. The process was undone after she was put in jail. Revenge: Her plan in her second appearance revolves around this. Her plan? Create a new line of clothes that literally crushes people to death. The only thing that saves the people wearing them is steam.

characters.name: Mandy Luxe
characters.description: Beverly Hills High's residentAlpha Bitch. Alpha Bitch: She is a textbook case of this trope (contrasting Clover's moreLovable Alpha Bitch). Extra points for being shallow. Ambitious, but Lazy: She wants to be famous without doing any sort of work. Annoying Laugh: Mandy has areallyannoying laugh. It sounds like a goat's bleating. Asshole Victim: Mandy becomes this every time she is kidnapped by theVillain Of The Week, to Clover's annoyance. This is most prominent in "Ski Trip" and "Grabbing the Bully by the Horns".

characters.name: Arnold Jackson
characters.description: Drunk with Power: Happened once when he accidentally foundCats Eye Emeraldtodrain people's cool aurainto himself, nerdifying the victims. Even when Sam warned him the effects wouldn't last, that just had Arnold go into his scheme to drain the people of Beverly Hills of their cool aura to get as much as he could. It led to him fighting another Villain of the Week for control of the Emerald until a beam from the ring got reflected back at it, and took out the magic, undoing the draining of others, and returning Arnold to his normal self. The Glasses Come Off: When he gets the ring and gets into the gym, he takes off his glasses. He then showed off his boosted abilities in a game of dodgeball. But that was a hint of hisStart of Darkness(he later nerdifies offscreen) and we next see him with anEvil Makeover(black leather jacket, open white shirt, and grey slacks) before nerdifying Clover as well. Informed Flaw: Is said to be undesirably ugly, but whenThe Glasses Come Offand he loses his freckles, he’s not much different than most of the guys the girls swoon over. Put on a Bus: Arnold leaves the show as he leaves to a different college. Redheads Are Uncool: A redhead nerd who's one of the most unpopular students and a frequent bullying target.

characters.name: David
characters.description: The Ace: He loves the arts, guitar playing, poetry, painting, etc. Ambiguously Brown: He's notieceably tanned skinned. Clueless Chick-Magnet: He has no idea all three of the main girls (and theirarchenemy) have a crush on him. Curtains Match the Window: He has brown hair to match his brown eyes. Like Brother and Sister: True to hisClueless Chick-Magnetnature, he says he and Sam are like siblings, unaware that she likes him as more than a brother.

characters.name: Dominique Leeland and Caitlin Jones
characters.description: Ambiguously Brown: Caitlin's this—with her green eyes and dark skin, she can be a dark-skinned Caucasian woman, a light-skinned South Asian or Middle Eastern woman, a mixed-race woman etc. The Bus Came Back: They return in season 7. Girl Posse: They both serve asValley GirlBeta Bitchesto Mandy and are easily just as mean, rude and snobby to people as Mandy is. Put on a Bus: They stopped appearing after "Evil Graduation" due to going to different colleges. Satellite Character: Other than being Mandy's friends and occasional rivals to Sam (for Dominique) and Alex (for Caitlin)Dominique and Caitlin don't really add much to the story.They haven't been seen or mentioned since "Evil Graduation" (the first episode of the fifth season) and are ultimately replaced by Mandy's cousin, Mindy, who's basically just Mandy with blonde hair, a darker tan and a thick Southern accent.

characters.name: Mindy Luxe
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: Mindy's basically just a blonde and tanned clone of Mandy with a thick Southern accent,which drifts into Canadianat times. Bare Midriffs Are Feminine: She has anAlpha Bitchpersonality, and tends to wear outfits that doesn't cover her stomach. Beauty Is Bad: Like her cousin, she is insufferable, but is an attractive young lady. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She hasn't been seen or mentioned since "Totally Icky" (the second-to-last episode of the fifth season), and Mindy's disappearance is especially jarring since she appeared in almost every episode of Season 5 (usually alongside her cousin). Ms. Fanservice: Just as beautiful like her cousin and the spies.

characters.name: Trent
characters.description: A Day in the Limelight: In "Trent Gone Wild" where he isTemporarily a Villain. Eerie Pale-Skinned Brunette: A male example. Extreme Doormat: Is constantly bossed around by Mandy. Forced Transformation: Transforms into a human-scorpion hybrid in "Trent Goes Wild" when his mind wipe goes wrong. The Intern: For Mandy in season 6.

characters.name: Professor Plunkett
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: He is very flamboyant and wears a giant pink feather boa. Badass Normal:Despite being a fashion teacher, Professor Plunkett is able to deactivate two of the giant statues by himself when he observes from the spies and Jerry that the key can stop the statues attacking his students. As soon as Jerry falls with the key, he quickly rushes over to retrieve it and uses it on the two remaining status in quick succession. Big Damn Hero:In the last episode, when he sees the key is able to disable the giant statues, he rushes to grab it and turn off the two that were attacking his students. Catchphrase: "FABULOOOOOOUS!" Funny Foreigner: Judging from his accent, he's presumably originally from France—he's passionate about fashion, has a rather flamboyant/over-the-top nature and even has a stereotypical French mustache.

characters.name: Bethannyy
characters.description: Cloudcuckoolander: She doesn't seem to find it strange to dress like a cowgirl in front of everyone. Genki Girl: She's very excitable and is always in a giddy mood. Smarter Than You Look: She can be seen as an overly cheeryDumb Blonde.... but she's also one of the few characters to be suspicious of the main trio as she questions their mysterious disappearances.

characters.name: Ingrid Yardstick
characters.description: Damsel in Distress: All we see of her in person is her being stolen by Maggie.

characters.name: Gabriella "Gabby" Simpson
characters.description: Action Mom: After receiving a spy training under the W.O.O.H.P.. Accidental Misnaming: In "Totally Busted", she repeatedly mispronounces Jerry's name. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: The Brunette in "Mommies Dearest," later the Redhead in "Totally Busted." Brainwashed and Crazy: In "Mommies Dearest". Fiery Redhead: Gabby seems to be more spitfire than her daughter.

characters.name: Stella Ewing
characters.description: Action Mom: After receiving spy training under the W.O.O.H.P. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: The Blonde in both "Mommies Dearest" and "Totally Busted." Brainwashed and Crazy: In "Mommies Dearest." Hospital Hottie: Looks like an older version of her daughter and is revealed to be a surgeon in the show's sixth season. Mama Bear: Jumps into action and convinces Jerry to become a spy with Gabby and Carmen when her daughter and her friends are in danger.

characters.name: Carmen Casoy
characters.description: Action Mom: After receiving a spy training under the W.O.O.H.P.. Blonde, Brunette, Redhead: The Redhead in "Mommies Dearest, later the Brunette in "Totally Busted." Brainwashed and Crazy: In "Mommies Dearest". Education Mama: In "Alex Gets Schooled" her and Alex's father enroll their daughter at Dorsal Academy in England after it was assumed that Alex had gotten straight F’s on her report card (although it later turned out that Alex had gotten A’s and B’s and that Mandy was the one who had gotten straight F’s). I Want Grandkids: A mild example. When she's not upset over Alex's grades, she's encouraging Alex to look for a boyfriend.

characters.name: Phoebe Luxe
characters.description: Education Mama: Seems to be this to some extent—in "Dental? More Like Mental!," Phoebe took away Mandy's credit cards and grounded her after discovering that she was apparently failing some of her classes. And in "Alex Gets Schooled," after it turns out that there was mix-up among some of the report cards at Bev High (like Alex and Mandy accidentally getting each other's report cards), Phoebe grounds Mandy after it turns out that Mandy had gotten straight-Fs.Phoebe:(to Mandy) You are grounded by the rest of the year, young lady, and that means, no dates!. Good Parents: While it's clear that Mandy's pretty spoiled by her parents, Phoebe (similar to Charlotte Pickles fromRugrats) isn't afraid to discipline her daughter when she really deserves it. SeeEducation Mamaabove. Granola Girl: She was a hippie back in the 1970s and still carries a bit of the distinction as an adult, at least in her debut episode when she's finally seen as an adult. Nice Girl: "Nice" is kind of stretch, but while she can be a bitsnobbyshe doesn't appear to be as rude and mean as her daughter. Screw the Rules, I Have Money!: Apparently so, as she's able to buy up a whole line of clothingbefore it's even out yet.

characters.name: Mrs. Lewis
characters.description: '50s Hair: In later episodes she is shown with a hairstyle not too dissimilar from Queen Elizabeth II. '70s Hair: Her first appearance had her with disheveled gray hair in a style from the 70s. Granny Classic: She has gray hair, wears old fashioned clothes and is very proper and picky about manners and etiquette. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: She was blonde during her youth and she had been a spy for the force of good. In the Blood: She claims that Jerry inherited all of his skills from her, and since she is still very skilled in her old age, it seems to be true.

characters.name: Mr. Casoy
characters.description: Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: He is constantly giving his daughter cutesy names, is very overly enthusiastic with giving her affection in public and even wore a t-shirt with her face on it, apparently not realizing that he was embarrassing her. Race Lift: He was white in "Alex Gets Schooled" but in season 6, he looks kind of like an older male-version of his daughter. Unnamed Parent: Unlike his wife, it's never revealed what his first name is. He's just called "Dad" by Alex.

characters.name: Mr. Simpson
characters.description: Fiction 500: Implied since Sam says that he and his wife (Sam's mother) already have "one of everything" which includes a lot of expensive, luxurious stuff like a personal mani-pedi robot and having his portrait done professionally in the Louvre. There's also the fact that his family lives in Beverly Hills, his daughter is able to go on many expensive shopping spree's without worry and many other minor examples. Happily Married: To his wife Gabby. Season 6's episode "The Wedding Crasher" had Sam trying to find the perfect gift for their 20th anniversary. Unnamed Parent: Like with Alex's dad, his name is never revealed in the series.

characters.name: Mr. Ewing
characters.description: The Ghost: Unlike with Sam and Alex's dads (who're both seen in person at some point in the series), Clover's dad is the only one who's never been seen in person at any point in the series—however, he has been mentioned (both directly and indirectly) and it's indicated that Clover's parents (like Sam and Alex's parents) are in fact married. Unnamed Parent: Just like Sam and Alex's dads, his name is never revealed.

characters.name: Norman "Normie" Ewing
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: He is always referred to as "Normie." Annoying Younger Sibling: More of an annoying younger cousin, but he enjoys antagonizing Clover. Spoiled Brat: His behavior in "Zooney World" where he is openly hostile and disrespectful to his cousin Clover and is always ready to get her in trouble with Stella. He thankfully gets a personality change after Clover uses a mind control helmet to make him forget she and the girls were spies...and make him a little nicer. Took a Level in Kindness: When he returns, he's a lot nicer to Clover without the Zoonie helmet (although he is still a little bratty). Ungrateful Bastard: At the end of "Zooney World," Clover's cousin Norman doesn’t even thank Clover and her friends for saving him. All he does is demand things and brag about how he would snitch to Clover’s mother due to the latter being grounded. This just leads to Clover wiping Norman's memories.

characters.name: Jazz Hands
characters.description: A mime themed villain who is determined to make mimes stay in the spotlight, with him as the leader of his "mime empire". Affably Evil: He's actually quite personable and charming despite being a bad guy, as shown by his stint asArc Villain. Arc Villain: Serves as main antagonist of the Season 5 Jazz Hands arc, as Sam goes undercover after his release from prison to try and discover what his new plan is. Everyone Hates Mimes: His motive for becoming evil is because he feels that mimes don't get the recognition he feels they deserve. Inflating Body Gag: Somehow can inflate himselfa laa slapstick cartoon character, and can even useBlow You Awayattacks with the air in his belly.

characters.name: Geraldine Husk
characters.description: A former W.O.O.H.P. applicant who was rejected for not being "goody-goody enough to make the cut". In retaliation, she formed S.P.I. as a way to put W.O.O.H.P. out of business. It turns out S.P.I. orchestrated the crimes they stopped so they could get the glory and provide a distraction so that Geraldine can rob the national banks. After the girls revealed her and S.P.I. to be a fraud, she's devoted to defeating them. Arch-Enemy: Geraldine has an intense personal and strange hatred of Clover and serves as the most personal and recurring antagonist matched against each her. Geraldine also goes out of her way to try and kill Clover. Arc Villain: Geraldine is the main antagonist of the Season 5 Blaine arc, having hired Blaine to get rid of Clover. Brainwashed and Crazy: She once kidnapped Clover and turned her into a cyborg under her control so she can take over the spy industry. Break the Haughty:She suffers this at the end of "Return of Geraldine" where, after the protagonists neutralize the submarine she stole from Blaine and tried to use to escape, she quickly goes from saying, "You haven't won yet!" to giving up and saying, "Okay! Maybe you have..." after being grabbed by their plane's robotic claw and she's shown looking sad and demoralized as it continues holding her out in the open, courtesy of Clover.

characters.name: Fabu
characters.description: Big Bad: Of theBig Damn Movie.

characters.name: Cyber Chac
characters.description: A technological villain who intends to infiltrate WOOHP-World for unknown reasons.Is eventually revealed to be a disguise for Mandy to prove herself worthy of being a spy, only to become an independent threat All Your Base Are Belong to Us:The AI versiontakes over WOOHP-World in the season finale. Ambiguous Gender: Until their unmasking, it was difficult to tell what gender they were. Big Bad: The most prominent threat for Season 7, and the villain of the finale. Exact Words: Their plan is to get inside WOOHP-World and meet the boss.Mandy simply wanted to do this task to prove she could make a good spy.

characters.name: Hayes
characters.description: A psychotic plane/submarine/blimp captain with a severe case of Celebrity Worship Syndrome. A very, very,verysevere case. Ax-Crazy: This guy is so obsessed with celebrities, he's willing to do anything to keep them in his menagerie. Such as use a super advanced jet to reverse the rotation and time on earth, flood the earth so that only he and his captive celebrities in his submarine are the only survivors and steal the talents of any celebrities he kidnaps in his blimp. I'm Your Biggest Fan: His primary motivation for wanting to kidnap celebrities. Loony Fan: Replace "loony" with "psychotic" and you've got this.

characters.name: The Granny
characters.description: A seemingly sweet old lady who is actually a master criminal who is always trying to rob banks with the help of her partners "Bubby" and "Papa". Affably Evil: The Granny is more than happy to give the girls cookies and other little gifts. Ascended Extra: All three of them make appearances inThe Amazing Spiez!as recurring villains. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She seems like a sweet and harmless old lady but it's all just a ruse as she is a very dangerous criminal and has the skills to back up her feared reputation at W.O.O.H.P.. The Bus Came Back: The only villain to return in series 7 (Marco Lumiere also appears, but he’s made aHeel–Face Turn).

characters.name: Marco Lumiere
characters.description: An insane film director out to assure the best possible performances, even by underhanded means. Arch-Enemy: Ends up forming this dynamic with Jerry, after using the W.O.O.H.P building as an evil lair and trying to trick him into getting revenge on some producers who screwed him over. Enforced Method Acting: His preferred method of film-making, mixed withFatal Method Acting. Heel–Face Return: In season 7, Jerry has helped him realise the error of his ways, and he subsequently went straight after serving his time. Paper-Thin Disguise: To trick Jerry into helping him, he put on a wig and some markup and assumed the aliasOcram Ereimul.

characters.name: Candy Sweet
characters.description: Her birth name being "Margaret Nussbaum," she's a villainous cheerleading coach who is determined to destroy the world of cheerleading out of revenge for being rejected by the Honeybees-cheerleading squad when she was in high school (Jerry reveals to the spies that Coach Sweet went to the same high school as the Honeybees, but had graduated ten years earlier). She's also an engineer in robotics, which is how she was able to create the Black Widow cheerleader war robots. Ax-Crazy: Her original plan with the Black Widows involved her having them murder everyone at the final competition seeing as a blow to the world of cheerleading. Cut Lex Luthor a Check: She's a robotics genius who wasted her engineering skills and tanked what probably could've been a very lucrative career in the name of petty, psychotic revenge. Disproportionate Retribution: She wants to destroy cheerleading in general because she was rejected by her high school's cheer squad. She never stopped to consider the idea of getting revenge directly against the members of the squad that rejected her, but instead victimizes a group of girls who weren't even in high school at the same time AND planned to murder hundreds of innocent people to prove a point. Evil Redhead: She has red hair.

characters.name: Diminutive Smalls
characters.description: A very, very SMALL mad scientist villain who tried to steal the world monuments by shrinking them down to his size, but he was thwarted by the spies. He was once a former W.O.O.H.P. agent who tried to make people stronger by shrinking them, only for it to backfire on him and his siblings. Chekhov's Gun: The reason he grew Mandy is because he saw her purse next to Clover's machine and grew her instead, thinking she was Clover. Had he not seen said purse, Mandy probably wouldn't have been involved in the plot at all. Revenge: His goal in "Attack of the 50 Foot Mandy," was to get revenge on the girls, particularly Clover. Shrink Ray: He uses one to steal monuments and shrink Clover.

characters.name: Dr. Gelee
characters.description: A mad scientist who is obsessed with chess and determined to freeze the entire world over. Has a particular grudge against Clover. And Now You Must Marry Me: He had taken Clover with him to make as his companion and "Ice Queen". The Blank: It is implied he suffers from face blindness, which would explain why he kidnapped Mandy instead of Clover, as Mandy's red snowsuit looks similar to Clover's red catsuit. Revenge: His motive in his second appearance is to get revenge on the girls (Clover in particularly) for both ruining his plans and rejecting his advances. Uncertain Doom: He is implied to have been killed when Mandy accidentally deflected a laser back at him.

characters.name: Dr. Gray
characters.description: A former psychiatrist who developed a device to swap people's personalities. "Freaky Friday" Flip: In his second appearance, he swapped minds with Jerry in order to take control of W.O.O.H.P.. Personality Swap: In his first appearance he used a device resembling a stopwatch used in hypnotherapy to swap the personalities (but not the minds) of his patients, and Jerry and Clover. The Shrink: He used to be one until he got sick of listening to his patients' problems and became aPsycho Psychologist.

characters.name: Sebastian Saga
characters.description: A former rock guitarist who lost his left arm in a freak pyrotechnics accident, resulting in him replacing it with a clawed prosthetic. Since then, he wanted revenge on the music industry for killing his career. Artificial Limbs: After he lost his left arm in a freak pyrotechnics accident, he had it replaced with a clawed metal prosthetic. Badass Longhair: Sebastian has long silver hair that hides the left side of his face. Mind-Control Music: His MO. In the first episode of the series, he tried to use rising pop star Ricky Mathis' music to take over the world in his name. Later in season two, he used a rage-inducing song to make people attending raves destroy the places the raves were taking place...which happened to be the Spies' favorite hangouts such as Alex's roller rink, Sam's art museum and Clover's mall. The grand finale would have been Beverly Hills High School. Starter Villain: The first bad guy of the series.

characters.name: Seth Toyman
characters.description: A toy maker who makes toys that come to life with military technology. Happy Ending Override: In his first appearance, he apologizes for what he’s done and gets nothing more than community service. In his next appearance, he hacked W.O.O.H.P. offscreen and got sent to jail.

characters.name: Boy Candy
characters.description: A boy band from the 1980s and Alex's favorite boy band. Their lead singer, T-Bone hatched a plan to bring themselves back into the spotlight by using a machine to swap faces with another boyband, Teencicle and play at the unity concert in Russia. Boy Band: Of the aging, has-been variety. Broken Pedestal: Alex declares them to no longer be her favorite boy band anymore, especially after their aging groupie swapped faces with her. Strangely enough, T-Bone becomes her favorite singer again in his second appearance after he was reformed. Didn't Think This Through: As Sam pointed out, they may have stolen Teencicle's youthful faces, but they didn't change their old and flabby bodies. To make matters worse, they spent so much time scheming, they forgot to practice for the unity concert, resulting in the crowd seeing right through them. Rebuilt Pedestal: They, or at least T-Bone, became this for Alex after spending time reflecting on past mistakes while in prison. Upon release, they decided to become famous again through honest work.

characters.name: Shirley
characters.description: A furious yoga teacher who tries to get revenge for being driven bankrupt by a rival studio. Disproportionate Retribution: She went bad just because she lost her business. Face–Heel Turn: She used to be the girls' and Mandy's yoga instructor until Kung Fu Fondu stealing the competition, as well as her anger problem, made everyone leave. Fiery Redhead: She has orange-red hair and has major anger issues. Mind Control: She uses mind control to get people to join her side. Said mind control also grants her minions powers normally found in Shonen Jump.

characters.name: Violet Vanderfleet
characters.description: An accomplished botanist, Violet experienced a string of unsuccessful romantic relationships, all of which ended in her being dumped. The breakups all soured her on romance, and men in general. In misguided revenge, she genetically engineered a hybrid of venomous flowers that could leave its victims in a zombie-like state, planning to use them to “zombify” the planet’s entire male population. Disproportionate Retribution: Just because she was dumped by a few men, Violet believes that ALL men are scum, and seeks to destroy all of them. Does Not Like Men: She hates men so much that she wants to poison every male on the planet. Expy: Shares some similarities withPoison Ivy, as they're both villainesses who usesplants as their way to battle the heroesand have alow opinion on men. Man-Eating Plant: Her chosen weapon. Her plants can not only poison victims, she says they can even swallow someone’s head whole.

characters.name: Ariel
characters.description: Brainwashed and Crazy: With the help of a magic belt, she can awaken the fighting spirit of the Sisterhood's descendants. Does Not Like Men: Hates all men and wants them to be destroyed. Female Misogynist: She also wants to destroy all weak women who are not part of the Sisterhood. Karma Houdini: The only villain who never got captured. Take Over the World: By destroying all men and non-chosen women, both metaphorical and literal in respective.

characters.name: Bertha Bombshell
characters.description: Evil Brit: She is British, and she is evil, so... Evil Redhead: She has orange hair and is evil. Never My Fault: She blamed the spies for her mutated state, never mind the fact that they tried to warn her of its effects. Old Flame: When Jerry realizes who Bertha truly is, he reveals to the spies that Bertha's an old girlfriend of his. Older Than They Look: She appears to be slightly older than the Spies but in reality, the fact was taking serum and was an old girlfriend of Jerry, marks her as over 50.

characters.name: Black Knight
characters.description: An unnamed knight theme villain who tried to use a time machine to overthrow a medieval king and take over his kingdom, which would have led to a chain reaction which would make him ruler of the world. Abhorrent Admirer: Clover does not reciprocate his feelings at all, which is understandable given his arrogant and misogynistic attitude. And Now You Must Marry Me: He is actually the first villain to do this as he was taken with Clover because of her good looks and tried to make her his "queen". Dark Is Evil: His armor is black and has an intimidating design,immediately establishing that he's a villain. Handsome Lech: He is quite dashing, but any love he wanted Clover to feel for him didn’t happen as she found out very soon, he was sexist, egotistical and arrogant.

characters.name: Bozette Slapstick
characters.description: Clownification: She uses her makeup to turn people into clowns against their will. Monster Clown: She's a clown who has gone mad.

characters.name: Carla Wong
characters.description: A Chinese video game designer who forces people to be live bait in her games. Asian Rudeness: She's an evil Chinese woman. Dragon Lady: She basically has this trope written all over her, from her design to her moniker.

characters.name: CHAD
characters.description: An AI assistant created by a bullied computer genius with the intent to harmlessly prank his creator's bullies, only to deal with them through violent means instead. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: He went from changing grades to launching nukes real fast. Bully Hunter: What he was created to be, he went off the deep end fast.

characters.name: Chet
characters.description: Beverly High's football captain who traps his fellow students inside a replica of the school to prevent them all from graduating and force them into reliving their school years forever. Cutting Corners: Lampshaded by the girls when they discover his replica school to be mostly made of cardboard props, considering the whole thing to be very low budget even by villain standards. Turns out most of the money went towards building a parade float that transforms into a tank. Didn't Think This Through: Part of his plan involves using a force field to keep the students trapped, except he fails to realize that doing so would cause a super greenhouse effect that puts everyone at risk of literally roasting to death. Fortunately, the girls shut it down before that happens. Glory Days: His whole motive boils down to him not wanting to move on from what he considers to be the best years of his life, unlike all his fellow classmates who would prefer to do the opposite. Psychopathic Manchild: The guy refuses to grow up and move on from his high school years, to the point of trapping himself and the rest of the students in a replica school in the middle of the desert.

characters.name: Cosmo Stratus
characters.description: A crazy woman who was kicked out of the space program, for failing to pass the psychological testing 15 times.She invented a machine to nullify the Earth's gravitational pull in order to "bring space to her" but was thwarted by the girls. Idiot Ball: Even if she's crazy, Cosmo is clearly skilled in rocket science but she never seems to consider the option that she could have just easily build her own rocket to send her to space instead of a gravity nullifying machine. Mad Scientist: Emphasis on the MAD. Never My Fault: She blames NASA from keeping her from achieving her dream of traveling to space because they failed her in the psychological test…never mind the fact that the only reason they kept failing her is because she is already visibly unstable. Psychopathic Womanchild: Doesn't get much more psychotic and petty than wanting to nullify the Earth's gravity just because NASA rejected her.

characters.name: Dr. Fox
characters.description: Didn't Think This Through: Dr. Fox gave several zoo animals human intelligence by mixing their DNA with his using a ray to allow them to get back to humans for caging them but didn't think that they could turn on him as well or have their own plans, which they do. Disproportionate Retribution: He not only wants to imprison humans in cages but also turn them into animals, even ones who are animal caretakers. A Taste of His Own Medicine: He gets betrayed by the same animals he liberated and gets turned into a dog by using his own DNA swapping ray against him. Well-Intentioned Extremist: He hates seeing animals into captivity and wants to liberate them, but by giving them human intelligence and caging up innocent humans and turning them into animals. What Happened to the Mouse?: He's nowhere to be seen after the spies go to stop the uplifted animals but it's likely he was arrested by WOOHP and turned back to normal.

characters.name: Dr. Inga Bittersweet
characters.description: A Swiss cookie maker who was part of the Happy Girls (a Girl Scout-style scouting organization) as a kid, but was kicked out for eating the cookies that she was supposed to be selling. To get revenge, she created "Passion Patties," mint-flavored chocolate cookies that are extremely addictive and make people go crazy for them (as well as making them extremely overweight in a very short time). Balloon Belly: Balloons up in size when Sam gives her a literal taste of her own medicine, becoming as big and addicted as Clover. Didn't Think This Through: She created a machine that would force feed people to death, but didn't bother adding a feature to stop them from simply spitting the food out of their mouths. Nor did she bother to confiscate the Spies' gadgets which prevented Sam and Alex from getting as fat as Clover. Disproportionate Retribution: Combined withNever My FaultandVillainous Glutton—since she ate the cookies instead of selling them, it's ultimately Inga's own fault that she got kicked out of the Happy Girls as a kid, but she wants to get revenge anyway. Herr Doktor: She's a Swiss scientist and she has a German accent (German's the most commonly spoken language in Switzerland).

characters.name: Eugene Snit
characters.description: Don't Tell Mama: Has a massiveBrawnhildaof a mother which he is terrified of. After beating him, Clover decides the best punishment is to simply tell his mom what he did. HisBig "NO!"when she comes in screaming his name shows just how effective that was. Evil Is Petty: Like nearly all the villains on this page his motivation is very petty. He was simply dumped by his girlfriend on Valentine's Day the year before. Humiliation Conga: Effortlessly beaten by Clover in a one on one bout, exposed in front of all the girls he was stringing along, was told on to his mom who burst in to see what he did, and to top everything off was arrested by W.H.O.O.P immediately afterwards. He's a video examplefor a reason! Intentional Heartbreaker: Strings alongevery single girl at Beverly Highjust so he can dump them at the Valentine's Day Dance. Misplaced Retribution: This series is infamous for villains, lashing out over minor things, but Eugene Snit takes the cake. His girlfriend dumped him on Valentine's Day the year before, so he decided to get revenge by installing dating booths that helped him to gather information on a girl's ideal boyfriend in Beverly Hills High. He then used a holographic disguise device that allowed him to change into that ideal boyfriend. Then he seduced all the girls at Beverly Hill High and stood them up by not showing up to the dance to break their hearts. So instead of seducing his ex-girlfriend and breaking up with her to break her heart, Eugene decides to seduce and break the hearts of a bunch of girls who had nothing to do with his breakup. What made this worse is that he did not even go to Beverly Hills High; his school is the Institute for Gifted Teens. While it still would have been petty and cruel, it would have made more sense for him to seduce and break the hearts of the girls at his own school.

characters.name: Fan Girl
characters.description: A spy-obsessed woman who kidnaps spies for her menagerie of living dolls. Living Doll Collector: After collecting every action figure, movie, comic book, and video game of all things spy and even starting an underground spy fan website,Fangirlgoes the extra mile in her fanaticism and starts stealing real spy gadgets before graduating to kidnapping real spies. Loony Fan: Self-explanatory.

characters.name: Farmer John
characters.description: A fruit and vegetable farmer who plots to turn humanity into human/plant hybrids out of hatred for those who live largely meat-eating lifestyles. Abusive Parents: Turning your own sons into plant monsters? Yeah, this guy isnotwinning any father of the year awards anytime soon. Artificial Hybrid: He uses a machine that can merge his victims with fruits and vegetables into monstrous hybrids. Irrational Hatred: Of people who largely eat meat and use animal products. His own sons are no exception.

characters.name: Felicity Fences
characters.description: A very spoiled heiress who kidnaps the world's hunkiest men to add as her collection and then force them to fight with her robot gladiators for her own amusement. It Amused Me: Her forcing her victims to fight her robots is solely because of this reason. Rich Boredom: Her entire motive for villainy is not because of revenge or conquest, it's only because she is bored in her luxurious lifestyle. Sadist: She outright kidnaps innocent men and force them to fight for their lives against her robots just for entertainment. Screw the Rules, I Have Money!: She believes that her father's money makes her above the law and even threatened to tell her father that W.O.O.H.P. arrested her.

characters.name: Felicia Mann
characters.description: An owner of a high-end wig-making company. It's revealed that the secret of her high-quality wigs is that they come from women that have been kidnapped and have their hair soaked in a special growth formula that also drains their life in the process. Bald of Evil: It turns out her enormous hair is actually a wig that hides her bald head. Cut Lex Luthor a Check: She created a working hair growth formula, which is particularly bad as she used it to quickly grow women's hair until they were almost dead, then selling the hair to be made into wigs. You know, the item that would become completely irrelevant overnight if a working hair growth formula existed. Evil Brit: The main villain of her episode and she's also from England. Ironic Name: Her last name means long hair, but she's actually as bald as a mango.

characters.name: Frankie Dude
characters.description: A formerly-renowned surfer who creates tsunamis to destroy beach resorts in order to restore them to their former, surfer-friendly glory. Agony of the Feet: One of his motivations for demolishing beach resorts is that he lost his pinky toe from a newly-built pier. Ambiguously Brown: He has dark skin that implies he is black, but has blond hair. Surfer Dude: One of the most prolific surfers in his time, and speaks in the lingo.

characters.name: Ice Solina
characters.description: An African-Hawaiian figure skater terrorist, Solina wants to freeze the world due to being too lazy to go somewhere cold to skate. High Hopes, Zero Talent: Despite her insistence that she’s destined to be a great figure skater, in practice, she’s shown to actually be pretty abysmal at it as she keeps falling down and many people note that she has little to no actual skating abilities. Lazy Bum: This mindset was the reason she became evil, was all because of her laziness to leave her beloved Hawaii to go to a cold part of the Earth to skate. Psychopathic Womanchild: Solina's rationale for freezing the world: she couldn't be bothered to leave Hawaii for somewhere cold to skate.

characters.name: John Smith
characters.description: A principal who is actually more than 800 years old, having discovered three Sumatran gems that can drain the life force out of people and give him eternal youth. Immortality Immorality: Has kept himself alive and young for 800 years by draining the life force of other people. Killed Off for Real: When the gem at the concert exploded in his proximity, Smithturns into nothing but a pile of dustin Sam's hand. Really Seven Hundred Years Old: Heck, he's even older than that! He's been around since the 12th century, draining the life energy out of people to preserve his youth. What Happened to the Mouse?: Smith found three gems that can give him his youth, but only one was destroyed, resulting in his death. It's unknown what happened to the other two.

characters.name: Kandinsky
characters.description: Nicknamed "The Great Kandinsky", he was once a renowed illusionist, but after the secrets to his magic/illusions were exposed, he faked his death and started using his stage magician skills to steal valuable art. Criminal Magician: He's a former professional stage magician who uses his skills to commit art theft. Faking the Dead: He supposedly drowned in a boat accident, but actually staged his death. Mind Control: Uses hypnosis to make his grandson, Gregor, his accomplice. Stage Magician: He used to be one, and he now uses all the skills he once used to perform to commit crimes and fight the spies.

characters.name: Kyle Katz
characters.description: A very handsome and charismatic jewel thief who had eluded W.O.O.H.P. for years and who only commits heists whenever the planets are aligned, which causes complete darkness. All three of the spies are taken with him because of his dashing good looks. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He seems like a kind, charming and personable man in front of the girls, but he's only pretending in order to make his escape. Distracted by the Sexy: He deliberately plays this trope in order to manipulate the girls in order to turn them against each other so he can carry out his plans. No-Nonsense Nemesis: He is basically what would happen if a criminal from the real world was dropped into theTotally Spies!universe. As he's targeting the Uzbekistan Pearl, the spies enter the vault to stop Katz while holding up said pearl. He just grabs the pearl, slams the vault door right in their faces, changes the lock code, and then leaves.

characters.name: Lady Luna
characters.description: A crazy astronaut in training who is obsessed with space and the zodiac, who was rejected and is furious about it. Light Is Not Good: She's a crazy woman with blonde hair and a blue spacesuit. Meaningful Name: "Luna" means moon.

characters.name: Lasputin Zero
characters.description: Didn't Think This Through: When Lasputin makes the trees carnivorous and bloodthirsty to defend themselves from loggers never once does he consider that they might look for more food or turn on him, both of which ends up happening. Even Evil Has Standards: Lasputin had no problem feeding loggers to his trees, but was disturbed when the trees turned to attack a city of innocent people.

characters.name: Logan Jay
characters.description: A renowned dentist who lost his license after a whitening treatment for the president's teeth went awry, now seeking revenge by kidnapping and brainwashing his former clients while arming them with super-powered dental implants. Depraved Dentist: Uses his dentistry skills to create soldiers to aid him in his revenge against those who wronged him. Never My Fault:Subverted. Dr. Jay insists that he gave the president specific instructions on how to use his special whitening solvent, but the latter didn't follow them correctly and chose to blame the former when it ended up ruining his teeth instead.

characters.name: Little Dude
characters.description: An aging skateboarder who seeks to turn the world into one big skate park to reclaim his former glory. Cut Lex Luthor a Check: The guy came up with a formula for creating instant asphalt, something that could've made him billions if he didn't waste it on building skate ramps trying to impress a bunch of kids. Ecocidal Antagonist: Makes it clear that he couldn't care less that his paving is destroying the environment, to the point of almost freezing a passing chameleon in asphalt in front of the spies. Glory Days: He claims to have once been hailed as the king of skateboarding before he was ridiculed for his moves being too old and basic, now seeking to reclaim his former glory even if he has to pave the entire world to do it. Mike Nelson, Destroyer of Worlds: Jerry eventually claims that if Little Dude isn't stopped soon, the latter's excessive paving will cause Earth to be thrown off its orbit and spiral out into the galaxy. The spies are unable to get him to listen about this, though they don't necessarily need him to.

characters.name: Maggie Trendset
characters.description: Cool Bike: Not exactly a bike, but her moped is equipped with a paint spraying function. She uses it to literally paint the entire city. Disproportionate Retribution: Pretty much the whole reason Maggie turned evil was because her designs kept being rejected and now wants tomake people notice her (and her designs)by kidnapping other interior designers. Evil Brit: Despite being American, she speaks with an accent similar toRarity. I Just Want to Be Special: She wants to become famous and well-known, but her awful taste in interior design keeps getting rejected. Meaningful Name: She wants to be a famous interior designer, but it's more of anIronic Namebecause nobody saw her as a trendsetter.

characters.name: Max Exterminus
characters.description: And Now You Must Marry Me: He called Alex his queen of all insects, having been captivated by her looks and her dangerous lifestyle as a spy. He transformed her into a human/cockroach-hybrid just like him (though not acompletetransformation) and claimed he and Alex will have larvae together, much to her disgust at the time. Et Tu, Brute?: He seemed genuinely hurt when Alex squirted bug spray in his face and left him to die. Killed Off for Real: After the rocket containing his bug venom began to crash, Max refused to let it go, claiming it to be his life's work and was seemingly killed when the rocket exploded on impact. Villainous Crush: He developed one on Alex, comparing her to a black widow spider: "You're dark, leggy, and I'm certain, quite dangerous."

characters.name: Milan Stilton
characters.description: A wealthy hotel heiress and the world's fifth richest person. She kidnaps other rich celebrities to rise to the top in terms of wealth. Unaware she was the culprit, the spies were sent to protect her but soon found out she is behind the abductions. No Celebrities Were Harmed: A not-so-subtle parody ofParis Hilton. Psycho Pink: She has long pink hair and she is very evil. Psychopathic Womanchild: She's a deranged woman who behaves more like a spoiled teenager. Rich Bitch: Wealthy and also happens to be an evil bitch. Even before she was revealed to be the villain, she made it no secret she is very rude and materialistic.

characters.name: Muffy Peprich
characters.description: A sorority girl who brainwashes other sorority girls in joining her own club after being rejected by various sororities. Psycho Pink: Her hair is purplish-fuchsia and she is evil. The Quincy Punk: She dresses like a stereotypical punk.

characters.name: Nadia
characters.description: Bad Boss: She clearly doesn't tolerate failure andthinks she's better than any other country. She aims to make sure Romania always wins, even if it meant using underhanded tactics. Misplaced Accent: Her accent sounds more Russian than Romanian. Named After Somebody Famous: Likely named after the most successful Romanian gymnast, Nadia Comăneci.

characters.name: O.P. Parents
characters.description: A group of parents of a seemingly perfect community that is secretly brainwashing their teenagers and were eventually stopped by the spies. '50s Hair: The head father wears his brown hair in a brylcreemed hairdo thatRonald Reaganwould envy. '60s Hair: The head mother wears her blonde wavy helmet held by an Alice band, coupled with a cocktail dress, making her look likeBetty Draper. Abusive Parents: The fact that they were trying to BRAINWASH their own children is just the tip of the iceberg with them. Control Freak: That is putting it very, VERY MILDLY. The O.P. stands for Oceanic Palisades, but in reality, it should stand for "overprotective parents".

characters.name: Professor Fremont
characters.description: A "spy reject" who plots to destroy the world as revenge against all the spy organizations who turned him away for his lack of actual skills. The Alleged Car: The "spaceship" he plans to use for escaping Earth's destruction, which is a car that has been poorly modified and is falling apart at the seams. Know-Nothing Know-It-All: His spy skills, which according to him largely consists of "mail order training and imaginary expertise". Manipulative Bastard: He poses as a professor at Malibu University teaching a course called "Espionage 101", tricking the girls into helping him steal a device to use in his revenge plan and causing them to become wanted criminals. The Spymaster:Subverted. He thinks he's this, but in reality his skills are so mediocre thatnospy organization in the world wanted anything to do with him.

characters.name: Salty Schooner
characters.description: A pirate-themed villain who tried to steal the WOOHP-Tanic and force Clover to be his "pirate queen". Ax-Crazy: He goes from wanting to steal the WOOHP-Tanic ship to try and FLOOD THE EARTH after he learns of the powerful laser on board. Love at First Sight: Experiences this once he sees Clover dressed in her pirate chic clothes. A Pirate 400 Years Too Late: He looks, dresses, talks and acts like a real pirate. Ruthless Modern Pirates: He comes from a long line of sea pirates and wants to use the WOOHP-Tanic as his new ship.

characters.name: Shelly Junglelove
characters.description: Expy: Her design is very similar toPoison Ivy. Evil Is Hammy: She raises her voice a lot. Plant Person: So much that plants are the only thing she wants. Man-Eating Plant: Her plants are huge and can possibly eat people.

characters.name: Simon Tucker
characters.description: An Australian/Irish man who hates shopping and malls, as he considers it "commercialist". Disproportionate Retribution: He is evil because his business was shut down by a rival and is now out for revenge. Mind Control: He uses mind control by putting hypnotic radios on people's ears. He then makes them wear green hats, matching pants, white tank tops and blue war paint when they join his army to vandalize stores. Misplaced Retribution: He now hates shopping malls but he never thinks about targeting just the one specific rival business that caused his own business to shut down. Never My Fault: He thinks the rival business is to blame for hisFace–Heel Turn.

characters.name: Stacy
characters.description: A student at Malibu University who kidnaps students and teachers to drain their intellect so she can add it to her own. Ambitious, but Lazy:Big time. She's smart enough to build an intellect-stealing machine, yet can't be bothered to actually study for her classes to avoid failing them. Brain Theft: Her Cranium Drainium is designed to steal the intellect of those inside it and add it to her own. Genius Ditz: She's apparently too airheaded to study, yet she's capable of building a giant machine capable of stealing intellect from other people.

characters.name: Sunny Day
characters.description: A former model who wants to cause global warming to force people to by her sunscreen. Alpha Bitch: She has shades of this: In the commercial, she mocks two men by calling them losers for not using her sunscreen. When ranting to the captured spies, she calls the modeling agency she was fired from mean. Ms. Fanservice: She was a model and her first appearance is in a commercial where she's posing in a bikini.

characters.name: Tuesday Tate
characters.description: An Australian woman who was once one of the top supermodels in the world—after getting attacked by a lion during a circus-themed modeling shoot, Tuesday got a robotic leg and gave up her job as a model. She eventually became the head of her own modeling agency called "Picture Perfect," which is headquartered in Australia. Eventually, she created a machine that makes "picture perfect" models by switching peoples' "perfect" body parts to dominate the modeling industry and get revenge. Artificial Limbs: She replaced her right leg with a metal one after getting attacked by a lion during a circus-themed modeling shoot gone horribly wrong. Evil Redhead: She has red hair. Not Even Bothering with the Accent: She's (presumably) Australian but has an American accent.

characters.name: Virtual Demon
characters.description: Remember the New Guy?: The spies apparently encountered and defeated them before, but this is the first (and only) episode they show up in. Meaningful Name: His name connects to his motives. Neat Freak: Obviously. Ambiguously Brown: She has dark skin. Blow You Away: She has power over wind.

characters.name: Wera Vann
characters.description: Action Fashionista: An evil example since she's one of the villains. Idiot Ball: Combined withEvil Is Petty—to put it as simply as possible, Wera's entire motivation for becoming a villain is because she's mad that the wedding dresses she designed were only worn once before basically being locked away in a closet forever, never to be worn again. She doesn't seem to get (or is possibly just outright ignoring the fact) that, traditionally, a wedding dress isn't supposed to be worn by anyone for anything other than by a bride for her wedding.She also doesn't seem to consider that, if she wanted her designs to be worn more than oncethat badly, she can just design stuff other than wedding dresses—after all, there's plenty of other types of clothing that people wear on a more frequent basis than a wedding dress. Light Is Not Good: She wears pink and fuchsia, but is the opposite of sugar, spice, or anything nice. Not Even Bothering with the Accent: She's supposed to be British, but has an American/Canadian accent (unless she's an American who moved to England).

characters.name: Wink Weatherdale and Margie Clarkland-Krewitz
characters.description: A couple who run a game show that steals intelligence from its contestants to make them seem smarter. Ambiguously Brown: Wink has tanned skin. Ambiguously Jewish: Margie, what with her New York accent and surname. Beehive Hairdo: Margie has this. Brooklyn Rage: Margie has a New York accent, and she tries to kill the spies (by putting them in a suffocating booth) to keep her stolen smarts.
